points: Central store of identities (e.g. LDAP, Active Directory).
Directories (LDAP, Active Directory) centralise identities and groups.

subs.title: Identity Governance and Administration
points: Access requests, approvals, certifications and SoD checks.
IGA automates access requests, approvals, recertification and SoD checks.

subs.title: Identity as a Service
points: Cloud-delivered identity and SSO services.
IDaaS provides cloud-based identity, SSO and MFA.

subs.title: System Access Permission
points: Access granted by data owners on need-to-know and least privilege.
Access is granted by data owners on need-to-know and least privilege.

subs.title: Types of Access Controls
points: Mandatory (MAC) vs discretionary (DAC); role-based.
MAC: system-enforced labels. DAC: owner decides. RBAC: rights through roles.

subs.title: Information Security and External Parties
points: Third-party access needs contracts, risk assessment and monitoring.
Third parties need contracts with security clauses, risk assessment and monitored access.

subs.title: Digital Rights Management
points: Controls use and copying of digital content after distribution.
DRM controls use, copying and printing of digital content after distribution.

subs.title: Logical Access
points: Paths of access and exposures; controls over each path.
Logical access paths: network, remote, console, operator and application access.

subs.title: Access Control Software
points: Enforces identification, authentication and authorisation.
Access control software identifies, authenticates, authorises and logs access to resources.

subs.title: Logon IDs and Passwords
points: Unique IDs, strong passwords, lockout, no sharing; MFA preferred.
Unique IDs, strong passwords, lockout after failed attempts, no sharing, secure storage (hashed).
MFA for privileged and remote access.

subs.title: Remote Access Security
points: VPN, MFA, device checks, logging.
Remote access via VPN with MFA, device checks and logging.

subs.title: Biometrics
points: FAR, FRR, EER; enrolment and template protection.
Physical: fingerprint, palm, hand geometry, iris, retina, face. Behavioural: signature, voice, keystroke.
FAR (security), FRR (convenience), EER for comparison.
subs.tip: High-security sites focus on a low FAR.

subs.title: Naming Conventions for Logical Access Controls
points: Consistent names for resources and IDs support control and auditing.
Consistent naming of IDs and resources supports clear access rules and audit.

subs.title: Federated Identity Management
points: Trust between organisations using SAML/OIDC.
Federation lets users from one organisation access another’s services using SAML or OIDC trust.

subs.title: Auditing Logical Access
points: Review access paths, provisioning, reviews, privileged accounts and logs.
Review access paths, provisioning, reviews, privileged access, password settings and log monitoring.

sections.title: Network and Endpoint Security
sections.summary: Explains securing networks and devices with layered controls.
points: Firewalls (packet filter, stateful, application/proxy, next-generation) and DMZ architectures.
IDS/IPS, network segmentation, VPNs, NAC, wireless security.
Endpoint protection: hardening, EDR/anti-malware, patching, device encryption.

terms.d: Screened subnet between the internet and the internal network for public-facing servers.

auditor: Review firewall rule sets for unnecessary or overly permissive rules.
traps: A screened subnet (DMZ) is more secure than a single firewall.

subs.title: IS Network Infrastructure
points: Components and architecture of the organisation’s network.
Network infrastructure includes LAN, WAN, wireless, devices and services.

subs.title: Enterprise Network Architectures
points: Client-server, multi-tier, cloud and hybrid designs.
Architectures: client-server, multi-tier, cloud, hybrid; each changes trust boundaries.

subs.title: Types of Networks
points: PAN, LAN, WAN, MAN, SAN.
PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, SAN differ by scope and purpose.

subs.title: Network Services
points: DNS, DHCP, directory, email, file and print services.
Services: DNS, DHCP, directory, email, file and print; each needs hardening.

subs.title: Network Standards and Protocols
points: TCP/IP, OSI reference, IEEE standards.
TCP/IP and OSI models; IEEE 802 standards for LAN and wireless.

subs.title: Virtual Private Networks
points: Encrypted tunnels for remote access, intranet and extranet connections.
VPN types: remote access, intranet (site-to-site), extranet; protocols include IPsec and TLS.

subs.title: Network Attached Storage
points: Shared storage on the network; needs access control and backup.
NAS provides shared file storage; protect with access control, encryption and backup.

subs.title: Content Delivery Networks
points: Distributed servers improve performance and absorb DDoS.
CDNs cache content close to users and help absorb DDoS attacks.

subs.title: Network Time Protocol
points: Synchronised time is essential for log correlation and forensics.
NTP keeps clocks synchronised for logs, authentication (e.g. Kerberos) and forensics.

subs.title: Applications in a Networked Environment
points: Web, client-server, middleware, APIs and their risks.
Networked applications (web, APIs, middleware) need secure coding, authentication and encryption.

subs.title: Network Infrastructure Security
points: Device hardening, segmentation, monitoring, change control.
Harden devices, segment networks, control changes, monitor traffic and restrict management access.

subs.title: Firewalls
points: Packet filter, stateful, application/proxy, NGFW; screened subnet (DMZ) designs.
Packet filter: headers only. Stateful: tracks sessions. Application/proxy: inspects content. NGFW: adds application awareness and IPS.
Designs: screened host, dual-homed, screened subnet (DMZ).
subs.tip: A DMZ with two firewalls is the most secure common design.

subs.title: Unified Threat Management (UTM)
points: Single appliance combining firewall, IPS, anti-malware, filtering.
UTM combines firewall, IPS, anti-malware and filtering; simpler but a single point of failure.

subs.title: Network Segmentation
points: Separate zones to limit spread of attacks.
Segmentation (VLANs, firewalls, micro-segmentation) limits lateral movement.

subs.title: Endpoint Security
points: Hardening, EDR/anti-malware, patching, encryption, device control.
Endpoint controls: hardening, EDR/anti-malware, patching, encryption, device control, host firewall.

sections.title: Data Loss Prevention
sections.summary: Covers detecting and preventing unauthorised data exfiltration.
points: DLP covers data at rest, in motion and in use (endpoint, network, cloud).
Effective DLP depends on data classification and tuned policies.
Alerts need triage and response processes.

terms.d: Tools and processes that detect and block sensitive data leaving authorised boundaries.

auditor: Check DLP rules map to classification and that alerts are investigated.
traps: Classification must exist before DLP can work well.

subs.title: Types of DLPs
points: Network, endpoint, storage/discovery and cloud DLP.
Network DLP, endpoint DLP, storage/discovery DLP and cloud DLP (often via CASB).

subs.title: Data Loss Risk
points: Accidental and malicious leakage via email, web, USB, cloud.
Leakage can be accidental (misdirected email) or malicious (insider theft).

subs.title: DLP Solutions and Data States
points: Data at rest, in motion and in use.
Data at rest (stored), in motion (network) and in use (endpoint) need different controls.

subs.title: DLP Controls
points: Policies to monitor, warn, block or encrypt.
Actions: monitor, alert, block, quarantine or encrypt.

subs.title: DLP Content Analysis Methods
points: Rule/regex, fingerprinting, exact data matching, statistical, categories.
Methods: rules/regex, database fingerprinting, exact data matching, partial document matching, statistical analysis, categories.

subs.title: DLP Deployment Best Practices
points: Start with classification, pilot, tune, phase in blocking.
Classify data first, start in monitor mode, tune policies, then enforce gradually.

subs.title: DLP Risk, Limitations and Considerations
points: False positives, encrypted traffic, privacy concerns, cost.
Limitations: false positives, encrypted traffic, privacy concerns, cost and staff effort.

sections.title: Data Encryption
sections.summary: Explains symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hashing and digital signatures.
points: Symmetric (AES): fast, key distribution is the challenge.
Asymmetric (RSA, ECC): public/private keys enable key exchange and signatures.
Hashing provides integrity; digital signatures provide integrity, authentication and non-repudiation.
Key management (generation, storage, rotation, destruction) is critical.

terms.d: Sender cannot deny sending: achieved with the sender’s private key signature.

auditor: Review key management procedures and protection of private keys.
traps: Confidentiality: encrypt with the recipient’s public key.

subs.title: Elements of Encryption Systems
points: Algorithm, key, key length; strength depends on key management.
Elements: algorithm, key, key length; secrecy of the key, not the algorithm, protects data.

subs.title: Link Encryption and End-to-End Encryption
points: Link encrypts per hop; end-to-end protects data from sender to receiver.
Link encryption protects each hop; end-to-end protects data from sender to recipient.

subs.title: Symmetric Key Cryptographic Systems
points: One shared key (e.g. AES); fast; key distribution problem.
Same key encrypts and decrypts (e.g. AES); fast; key distribution is the challenge.

subs.title: Public (Asymmetric) Key Cryptographic Systems
points: Key pairs (RSA); encryption and signatures; slower.
Public/private key pairs (e.g. RSA); public key for confidentiality to the owner, private key for signatures.

subs.title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography
points: Strong security with shorter keys; suits mobile devices.
ECC gives equal strength with shorter keys, useful for mobile and constrained devices.

subs.title: Quantum Cryptography
points: Quantum key distribution; quantum computing threatens current public-key algorithms.
Quantum computers threaten current public-key algorithms; post-quantum algorithms are being adopted.

subs.title: Homomorphic Encryption
points: Compute on encrypted data without decrypting.
Allows computation on encrypted data, useful for privacy-preserving processing.

subs.title: Digital Signatures
points: Hash signed with sender’s private key: integrity, authentication, non-repudiation.
Hash signed with sender’s private key; verified with sender’s public key.
Provides integrity, authentication and non-repudiation, not confidentiality.
subs.tip: Non-repudiation = sender’s private key.

subs.title: Digital Envelope
points: Data encrypted with a symmetric key, which is encrypted with the recipient’s public key.
Symmetric key encrypts the message; recipient’s public key encrypts the symmetric key.

subs.title: Applications of Cryptographic Systems
points: TLS, IPsec, S/MIME, secure email and file encryption.
TLS, IPsec, S/MIME, PGP, SSH and disk encryption apply cryptography to real systems.

subs.title: Kerberos
points: Ticket-based network authentication using a trusted key distribution centre.
Kerberos uses tickets from a trusted key distribution centre; needs synchronised clocks.

subs.title: Secure Shell
points: Encrypted remote login and file transfer.
SSH replaces insecure Telnet/FTP with encrypted remote access and file transfer.

subs.title: Domain Name System Security Extensions
points: DNSSEC signs DNS data to prevent spoofing.
DNSSEC signs DNS records so resolvers can detect spoofed responses.

subs.title: Email Security
points: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, encryption and filtering.
SPF, DKIM and DMARC help prevent spoofing; S/MIME or PGP encrypt and sign email.

sections.title: Public Key Infrastructure
sections.summary: Covers certificates, certificate authorities and trust.
points: CA issues certificates; RA verifies identity; CRL/OCSP show revocation.
Certificates bind a public key to an identity; trust chains up to a root CA.
Protecting the CA private key is paramount.

terms.d: Certificate revocation list.

auditor: Check certificate lifecycle management and expiry monitoring.
traps: Compromise of the CA private key undermines all issued certificates.

subs.title: Digital Certificates
points: Bind public keys to identities; issued by CAs.
X.509 certificates bind a public key to an identity, signed by a CA.

subs.title: Key Management
points: Generate, distribute, store, rotate and destroy keys securely.
Key lifecycle: generation, distribution, storage (e.g. HSM), rotation, archival and destruction.

subs.title: Certificate Revocation
points: Revoke compromised or invalid certificates.
Certificates are revoked when keys are compromised or details change.

subs.title: Certificate Revocation List
points: Published list of revoked certificates; OCSP gives real-time status.
CRLs list revoked certificates; OCSP gives real-time status.

subs.title: PKI Infrastructure Risk
points: CA compromise, weak RA checks, expired certificates.
Risks: CA key compromise, weak registration checks, expired certificates, poor key storage.

subs.title: Audit Procedures for PKI
points: Review CA policies, key protection, certificate lifecycle.
Review certificate policies, CA key protection, registration procedures and lifecycle monitoring.

sections.title: Cloud and Virtualized Environments
sections.summary: Explains cloud service and deployment models, shared responsibility and virtualisation risks.
points: Service models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS; deployment: public, private, hybrid, community.
Shared responsibility: provider secures the cloud; customer secures configuration, identities and data.
Assurance: SOC reports, certifications, right-to-audit, data location, exit plans.
Virtualisation: protect the hypervisor, control VM sprawl, isolate workloads.

terms.d: Division of security duties between cloud provider and customer.

auditor: Review cloud configurations and IAM, not just the provider’s certificates.
traps: Accountability for data stays with the customer.

subs.title: Virtualization
points: Hypervisors host multiple VMs; protect hypervisor and isolate VMs.
Type 1 (bare-metal) and Type 2 (hosted) hypervisors; protect and patch the hypervisor.
Risks: VM sprawl, VM escape, insecure templates.

subs.title: Virtual Circuits
points: Logical connections over shared networks.
Virtual circuits are logical paths across shared networks.

subs.title: Virtual Local Area Network
points: Logical segmentation of a LAN at layer 2.
VLANs segment networks logically; protect against VLAN hopping.

subs.title: Virtual Storage Area Networks
points: Logical partitions of a SAN.
VSANs partition storage networks for isolation and management.

subs.title: Software-Defined Networking
points: Central controller programs the network; protect the controller.
SDN centralises network control; the controller must be strongly protected.

subs.title: Containerization
points: Lightweight isolation (e.g. Docker); secure images and orchestration.
Containers share the host kernel; secure images, registries and orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes).

subs.title: Secure Cloud Migration
points: Plan security, data protection and compliance before moving to cloud.
Plan data classification, legal requirements, IAM and encryption before migrating.

subs.title: The Shared Responsibility Model
points: Split of duties between provider and customer by service model.
IaaS: customer manages OS and up. PaaS: customer manages apps and data. SaaS: customer manages data and access.
subs.tip: The customer is always accountable for its data.

subs.title: Key Risk in Cloud Environments
points: Misconfiguration, weak IAM, data location, vendor lock-in, insecure APIs.
Misconfiguration, weak IAM, insecure APIs, data residency, lock-in and provider failure.

subs.title: DevSecOps
points: Security automated within CI/CD pipelines.
Integrate security testing (SAST, DAST, dependency checks) into CI/CD pipelines.

sections.title: Mobile, Wireless and Internet of Things Devices
sections.summary: Covers securing mobile devices, wireless networks and IoT.
points: Mobile: MDM, encryption, remote wipe, app control, BYOD policy.
Wireless: strong encryption (WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise), rogue AP detection.
IoT: change defaults, patch firmware, segment networks, inventory devices.

terms.d: Mobile device management.

auditor: Check BYOD policy enforcement and lost-device procedures.
traps: Remote wipe and encryption are key for lost or stolen devices.

subs.title: Mobile Computing
points: Smartphones and tablets accessing corporate data.
Mobile devices extend access but are easily lost and connect to untrusted networks.

subs.title: Mobile Device Threats
points: Loss/theft, malicious apps, insecure networks, data leakage.
Threats: loss/theft, malicious apps, insecure Wi-Fi, outdated OS, data leakage.

subs.title: Mobile Device Controls
points: Encryption, passcodes, remote wipe, app control.
Controls: device encryption, passcodes, remote wipe, app whitelisting, OS updates.

subs.title: Mobile Device Management
points: Central enforcement of mobile policies.
MDM enforces policies centrally and can containerise corporate data.

subs.title: Bring Your Own Device
points: Policy, containerisation, user agreement, privacy considerations.
BYOD needs a policy, user agreement, containerisation and respect for privacy.

subs.title: Internet Access on Mobile Devices
points: Risks of public Wi-Fi; use VPN and secure DNS.
Public Wi-Fi risks: interception and rogue hotspots; use VPN.

subs.title: Audit Procedures for Mobile Devices
points: Review MDM coverage, policies and lost-device handling.
Review MDM coverage, policy enforcement, lost-device process and app controls.

subs.title: Mobile Payment Systems
points: Tokenisation, secure elements, fraud monitoring.
Use tokenisation, secure elements and fraud monitoring for mobile payments.

subs.title: Wireless Networks
points: WPA2/WPA3, enterprise authentication, rogue AP detection.
Use WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise, strong authentication, rogue AP detection and segmentation of guest Wi-Fi.
subs.tip: WEP is broken; hiding SSIDs is not security.

subs.title: Internet of Things
points: Default credentials, weak patching; segment and inventory devices.
IoT risks: default credentials, weak patching, insecure protocols.
Controls: inventory, segmentation, credential changes, firmware updates.

sections.title: Security Awareness Training and Programs
sections.summary: Explains building effective security awareness, training and education.
points: Continuum: awareness for all, training for roles, education for specialists.
Needs assessment, targeted content, regular delivery and measured effectiveness (e.g. phishing simulations).

terms.d: Ongoing activities to make people recognise and respond to threats.

auditor: Check completion rates and whether results change behaviour.
traps: Awareness is the best control against social engineering.

subs.title: The Information Security Learning Continuum
points: Awareness → training → education → professional development.
Awareness (all staff) → training (role-based skills) → education (specialists).

subs.title: Benefits of a Security Awareness, Training and Education Program
points: Fewer incidents, better reporting, compliance.
Benefits: fewer incidents, faster reporting, compliance, security culture.

subs.title: Approach to Security Awareness, Training and Education
points: Role-based, regular, engaging content.
Use varied methods: e-learning, simulations, briefings, reminders.

subs.title: Conditions for a Successful Program
points: Management support, measurement, relevance and repetition.
Needs management support, relevance, regular delivery and measurement.

subs.title: Conducting a Needs Assessment
points: Identify audiences, gaps and priorities.
Identify audiences, risks and knowledge gaps before designing content.

subs.title: Implementing an Awareness and Training Program
points: Plan, deliver, measure and improve.
Plan, deliver, track completion, test behaviour (e.g. phishing) and improve.

sections.title: Information System Attack Methods and Techniques
sections.summary: Covers attackers, motives and common attack techniques.
points: Threat actors: insiders, criminals, hacktivists, nation states.
Attacks: phishing, malware, ransomware, DoS/DDoS, man-in-the-middle, SQL injection, XSS, brute force, social engineering, salami, logic bombs.
Passive attacks (eavesdropping, traffic analysis) are hard to detect.

terms.d: Stealing tiny amounts from many transactions.

auditor: Map controls to the attack techniques most relevant to the organisation.
traps: Encryption is the best control against eavesdropping.

subs.title: Fraud Risk Factors
points: Pressure, opportunity and rationalisation (fraud triangle).
Fraud triangle: pressure, opportunity, rationalisation; controls reduce opportunity.

subs.title: Computer Crime Issues and Exposures
points: Financial loss, legal, reputation; perpetrators inside and outside.
Exposures: financial loss, legal repercussions, reputation damage, loss of competitive advantage.
Perpetrators: insiders, former employees, hackers, organised crime, nation states.

subs.title: Internet Threats and Security
points: Phishing, web attacks, network-based attacks.
Internet threats include phishing, web application attacks, DDoS and man-in-the-middle.

subs.title: Malware
points: Viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware; layered defences and backups.
Viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware, rootkits.
Defences: anti-malware/EDR, patching, least privilege, email filtering, backups.

sections.title: Security Testing Tools and Techniques
sections.summary: Explains vulnerability scanning, penetration testing and other security tests.
points: Vulnerability assessments find known weaknesses; penetration tests exploit them to show impact.
Test types: black, white, grey box; internal and external; red/blue/purple teams.
Tests require written authorisation, defined scope and rules of engagement.

terms.d: Agreed scope, limits and timing for a security test.

auditor: Check findings are tracked to remediation.
traps: Never test without written management approval.

subs.title: Objectives of Security Testing
points: Identify weaknesses and confirm controls work.
Security testing confirms controls work and identifies weaknesses before attackers do.

subs.title: Security Assessments and Security Audits
points: Assessments find weaknesses; audits compare against criteria.
Assessments look for weaknesses; audits compare against defined criteria and give assurance.

subs.title: Vulnerability Assessments
points: Scan for known vulnerabilities and prioritise fixes.
Scanners identify known vulnerabilities; results must be validated and prioritised.

subs.title: Penetration Tests
points: Simulate attacks; black/white/grey box; authorised scope and rules of engagement.
Phases: planning, discovery, attack, reporting.
Black box (no knowledge), white box (full knowledge), grey box (partial).
subs.tip: Always get written authorisation first.

subs.title: Threat Readiness/Information Security Teams
points: Red, blue and purple teams test and improve defences.
Red teams attack, blue teams defend, purple teams combine both to improve detection.

subs.title: Security Testing Techniques
points: Code review, fuzzing, configuration review, social engineering tests.
Techniques include code review, fuzzing, configuration review and social engineering tests.

subs.title: Security Operations Center
points: Monitors, detects and responds to security events.
A SOC monitors events 24/7, triages alerts and coordinates response.

subs.title: Security Testing Audit Procedures
points: Check testing is authorised, scoped and findings are remediated.
Check testing is authorised, scoped, independent and that findings are tracked to closure.

sections.title: Security Monitoring Logs, Tools and Techniques
sections.summary: Covers monitoring security events with logs, SIEM and related tools.
points: SIEM correlates logs and raises alerts; SOC teams triage.
Use cases, thresholds and tuning reduce false positives.
Log integrity and time synchronisation matter for investigations.

terms.d: Security operations center that monitors and responds to security events.

auditor: Check alert handling times and evidence of follow-up.
traps: Collecting logs without reviewing them gives little protection.

subs.title: Information Security Monitoring
points: Continuous monitoring of events to detect threats.
Continuous monitoring detects threats and policy violations in time to act.

subs.title: Intrusion Detection Systems
points: Network/host-based; signature, anomaly or behaviour-based detection.
NIDS monitors network traffic; HIDS monitors hosts.
Signature-based detects known attacks; anomaly-based detects deviations but has more false positives.

subs.title: Intrusion Prevention Systems
points: In-line systems that block detected attacks.
IPS sits in-line and blocks attacks; risk of blocking legitimate traffic.

subs.title: Audit Logging in Monitoring System Access
points: Log access events, review regularly, protect logs.
Log successful and failed access, privilege use and changes; review regularly.

subs.title: Protecting Log Data
points: Restrict access, integrity checks, central storage, retention.
Protect logs with restricted access, integrity checks, central storage and retention rules.

subs.title: Security Information and Event Management
points: Collects and correlates logs, generates alerts.
SIEM aggregates and correlates logs, generates alerts and supports investigations.

subs.title: Security Monitoring Tools
points: SIEM, IDS/IPS, EDR, network analytics.
Tools: SIEM, IDS/IPS, EDR, NDR, vulnerability scanners, file integrity monitoring.

sections.title: Security Incident Response Management
sections.summary: Explains preparing for and handling security incidents.
points: Phases: preparation, detection/identification, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned.
Roles, escalation paths, communication and legal/regulatory notification are defined in advance.
Incidents are classified by severity to drive response.

terms.d: Limiting the spread and impact of an incident.

auditor: Check plans are tested and lessons learned are implemented.
traps: Containment comes before eradication.

subs.title: Incident Response Process
points: Prepare, detect, contain, eradicate, recover, learn.
Preparation, detection/analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, post-incident review.

subs.title: Computer Security Incident Response Team
points: Trained team with defined authority and contacts.
A CSIRT has defined roles, authority, contacts and trained members.

subs.title: Incident Response Plan
points: Documented procedures, roles, escalation and communications.
The IR plan defines procedures, escalation, communication and legal/regulatory notification.

subs.title: Security Orchestration, Automation and Response
points: SOAR automates routine response actions using playbooks.
SOAR automates repetitive response steps using playbooks to speed containment.

sections.title: Evidence Collection and Forensics
sections.summary: Covers collecting and preserving digital evidence so it is admissible.
points: Identify, preserve, collect, examine, analyse, report.
Work on verified forensic images (hash values), never the original.
Maintain chain of custody; involve legal counsel.

terms.d: Bit-for-bit copy of storage verified by hash.

auditor: Check procedures exist before an incident occurs.
traps: Powering off or browsing a suspect machine can destroy evidence.

subs.title: Types of Investigations
points: Criminal, civil, regulatory and internal investigations.
Investigations may be criminal, civil, regulatory or internal; each has evidence requirements.

subs.title: Types of Computer Forensics
points: Disk, memory, network, mobile and cloud forensics.

subs.title: Phases of Computer Forensics
points: Identify, preserve, analyse, present.
Identify, preserve, analyse, present; document every step.

subs.title: Audit Considerations
points: Check readiness procedures and evidence handling.
Auditors check forensic readiness, policies and evidence-handling procedures.

subs.title: Computer Forensic Techniques
points: Imaging, hashing, timeline analysis, data carving.
Imaging with write blockers, hashing, timeline analysis, file carving.

subs.title: Computer Forensics Tools
points: Specialised tools for imaging and analysis; validated before use.
Use validated tools; record versions used.

subs.title: Chain of Custody
points: Record every transfer of evidence to keep it admissible.
Record who handled evidence, when and why, from collection to court.

subs.title: Best Practices to Secure Digital Evidence
points: Work on copies, verify hashes, secure storage, document everything.
Work on copies, verify hashes, store securely, limit access, document everything.
subs.tip: Never analyse the original evidence.
